subject: Re: Proposal for scaled liquidated-damages, escrow, and conditional termination
messages:
From: Peter Langston <plangston@biomedco.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Rossi <erossi@biomedco.com>, BiomedCo Legal <legal@biomedco.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:04:00Z
Subject: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

Mina — thanks for a productive demo last week. We ran the pilot through our reliability model and have a new ask from Legal and procurement. They want entitlement beyond service credits for systemic degradation that materially impacts patient workflows.

High-level request: a scaled liquidated damages (LD) formula tied to estimated monthly ARR impact (BiomedCo's model is attached: SLA_Risk_Model.xlsx). The structure they're asking for:
- Tier 1 (minor latency spikes): credits up to 5% of monthly invoice
- Tier 2 (sustained degraded P95 latency beyond 15% of SLA windows): cash LD = 10% of impacted month's MRR
- Tier 3 (incidents causing >72 hours cumulative severe degradation): fee-at-risk in escrow equal to 30% of 3-month MRR + right to terminate for convenience with 60 days notice and limited buyout equal to 6 months of fees.

They also want the escrow to be funded at contract signature with staged releases tied to passing SRE runbooks and a third-party availability audit annually.

We understand this is beyond your standard remedies; asking for an initial read and whether Redwood would consider a compromise (e.g., dedicated capacity with a capped escrow, or a staged LD tied to severity ladder). Attached is a one-page summary of the exact language Legal prefers (Requested_Term_Summary.pdf).

Peter
Director, Procurement — BiomedCo

--
Attachment: SLA_Risk_Model.xlsx (spreadsheet with estimated ARR impact by service tier)

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Langston <plangston@biomedco.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

Peter — thanks for sending the model and summary. Appreciate the clarity. High-level reaction before we loop Legal:

- We understand the need to reduce commercial exposure from outages that materially affect your product.
- Cash LDs and termination-for-convenience tied to availability are big asks for a hosted service; our standard approach is service credits with a capped liability and a remediation/transition playbook.

Proposed pragmatism we can consider now:
1) For the pilot, offer a capped fee-at-risk escrow of 15% of 3 months' committed spend (funded at signature) with staged declines over first 6 months contingent on observed SLOs and remediation playbooks.
2) Introduce a severity ladder and a formulaic credit+cash-mix: the majority of Tier 2 is credits; a limited cash component kicks in for repeat Tier 2 violations within a trailing 90-day window.
3) For Tier 3 catastrophic exposures (>72 cumulative hours), we can agree to a termination right, but with a transition assistance window and a capped buyout (proposed: 3 months' committed fees), not 6.

I'll run this with Legal and ops to validate feasibility (we need to align on escrow custodian options and an acceptable third-party auditor). Monica, can you run a quick ops feasibility on staged escrow release triggers? Karthik, please flag any absolute legal no-gos.

Mina
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_Initial_Response.docx

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-13T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

Quick ops note — escrow release triggers tied to SLOs are operationally workable but add bookkeeping and an annual audit burden. Options I see:
- Use a neutral escrow agent (low friction) and define objective telemetry metrics we already export to the Console for release conditions.
- Third-party audit yearly is OK, but add a 30-day cure period before any escrow draw.

If we go down the staged-release path, need to bake in a clause preventing simultaneous draw for unrelated incidents (i.e., incidents must be proven to affect BiomedCo's tenant).

M

From: Peter Langston <plangston@biomedco.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Rossi <erossi@biomedco.com>, BiomedCo Legal <legal@biomedco.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T15:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

Mina / Monica — that helps, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:
- The buyout cap is negotiable, but 6 months is the baseline for our board to greenlight sign-off for regulated customers.
- The 30-day cure window is fair, but their ask includes a clause allowing immediate partial draw for documented revenue impact while a cure is attempted (this is why they want the third-party auditor language).
- They're open to escrow held by a mutual custodian (we suggested EscrowCorp); they'd like the escrow funded at signature to avoid moving money after a post-signing incident.

Would Redwood consider a pilot with the following compromise?
A) Fund 20% of 3-month committed spend into escrow at signature.
B) Tiered releases quarterly tied to SLO pass rates; emergency partial draw available with auditor attestation and a 30-day backstop for remediation.
C) Termination right if cumulative severe (>72 hours) degradation persists over a rolling 3-month period, with a buyout equal to 4 months of committed fees.

We can accept a capped absolute liability relative to ARR but need the commercial certainty.

Peter

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Peter Langston <plangston@biomedco.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

On Wed, Jun 16, 2027 at 09:40 Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Mina — thanks for sending the model and summary. Appreciate the clarity. High-level reaction before we loop Legal:
> 
> - We understand the need to reduce commercial exposure from outages that materially affect your product.
> - Cash LDs and termination-for-convenience tied to availability are big asks for a hosted service; our standard approach is service credits with a capped liability and a remediation/transition playbook.

Folks — legal POV: absolute cash LDs tied to estimated ARR loss are a major exposure we generally avoid because they become proxy for customer downstream claims (we don't control their business losses). Strategy: move to a hybrid framework that limits cash exposure, requires narrow, objective incident definitions, and a mandatory remediation and arbitration pathway before termination.

Proposed legal counterterms to take to BiomedCo Legal:
1) Escrow accepted at signature but limited to 15% of 3 months' committed fees.
2) Emergency partial draw requires independent auditor attestation and mutual SRE verification. Draws are exclusively to cover direct fees/refunds to BiomedCo, not open-ended downstream damages.
3) Termination right only available if (a) three separate qualifying Tier 3 incidents occur within a rolling 90-day window OR (b) a single Tier 3 event continues for >120 cumulative hours despite remediation efforts. This tightens the customer's language.
4) Buyout capped at 3 months' committed fees; if customer insists on higher, require additional premium pricing/insurance.

I'll draft redline language with these guardrails. If BiomedCo needs a larger buyout, we should discuss a reserved-capacity add-on priced accordingly.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Peter Langston <plangston@biomedco.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Rossi <erossi@biomedco.com>, BiomedCo Legal <legal@biomedco.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Scaled LD proposal + escrow ask for pilot contract

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic counters. Elena will review Karthik's redlines and circulate a mark. Two quick asks from us to keep momentum:
1) Please confirm the neutral escrow agents Redwood will accept (we recommended EscrowCorp and CustodiaTrust).
2) Can Redwood commit to running a 30-day operational acceptance test after pilot onboarding to baseline observed SLOs before escrow release staging?

If we can get answers this week, Legal will prepare a counter-mark and we can move to DocuSign.

Best,
Peter
